finding.location: code/transfer_test.py lines 130-153 (chance floors and validity rule); SUMMARY.md lines 13-14, 21-25, 31-36
finding.description: The only comparisons are a constant predictor and a uniform random predictor, and the pass/fail rule is very lax (R_diff > max(0.15, 2 x constant) and median error < 86 deg). R_diff on these labels is driven mainly by coarse phase class, because about a quarter of RPE1 cells sit in one G1 cluster at 270-300 deg and the rest in S and G2/M arcs. A simple G1/S/G2M class call therefore scores as well as or better than the readouts. The summary reads 'Both transfer ... against 0.043 for a constant predictor' and 'recovers RPE1 phase' as evidence of a transferred phase readout, but these floors cannot tell a phase readout apart from a coarse marker-based classifier.
finding.evidence:
All computed inline with the package's own functions on RPE1, with no RPE1 labels used:
- Seurat-style 3-class call (G1/S/G2M from RPE1 module scores), each class mapped to its K562 class-mean angle: R_diff 0.869, median error 15.7 deg. That beats the model readout (0.789, 23 deg) and nearly ties the expression readout (0.878, 16 deg).
- Ridge fit on K562 using only the two module scores (S, G2M): transfer R_diff 0.961, median error 7 deg.
- 2-class predictor (G2M score > 0 -> 155 deg, else 285 deg): R_diff 0.646, 27 deg. It easily passes the rule (threshold 0.15 and 86 deg).
The model readout does carry some ordering within phase arcs (Spearman 0.70, 0.71 and 0.49 in three arcs), but the reported metric and floors do not show this.

grader_reason: I reproduced the numbers. A 3-class module-score predictor mapped to the K562 class means gets R_diff 0.869 and 15.7 deg. A 2-class predictor gets 0.646 and 27 deg. 729 of the 3,000 RPE1 cells (24%) fall in the 270-300 deg bin. But the key lists 'chance floor too lenient' as a possible false alarm. A constant at the target mean is the right label-free chance level. The marker-class baseline is itself a K562-to-RPE1 transfer built from the same markers that define the label. So it does not show the activation readout failed to transfer, or that 'recovers RPE1 phase' is false. The summary never claims the readout resolves phase more finely than a coarse class call. This is a request for stronger baselines, not a confirmed error in the headline.
posthoc_reason: The grader reproduced the baselines: a 3-class module-score call gives R_diff 0.869, a 2-class call gives 0.646, and both pass the lax gate. The finding itself reports within-arc ordering (Spearman 0.49-0.71). A coarse phase call is still a phase readout, and the summary claims only that both readouts transfer and recover RPE1 phase, never finer-than-class resolution, so no stated result is overturned.
